FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 2.

The brief facts relevant for disposal of the present petition are that on 26.12.2019, at about 08.10 PM, the deceased and two other persons were hit by a car bearing registration no. DL-7CR-0123 (in short "the offending vehicle") at Rithala Metro Station, near CISF Camp.

Deceased was taken to Dr.
BSA Hospital.
During the course of treatment, he was declared dead on 26.12.2019.
Respondent no.
1 was driving the car at the time of accident.
Respondent no. 2 is the registered owner of the offending vehicle and it was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident.
3. An FIR No. 338/2019, PS Budh Vihar, Delhi was registered U/s 279/337/304A IPC.

4. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and respondent no.2, and it is submitted that no such accident was MACT Case No. 301/2020 (FIR no. 338/19) Shahney Vijayan &
Anr. V. Sanjeev Kumar & Ors.
Page no. 2 of 17 caused by the offending vehicle.
Driver has nothing to do with the accident.
Injured was going in negligent manner and himself touched with the car.
The driver was having valid driving license.

The offending vehicle was insured with Liberty General Insurance Ltd vide Policy No.
211-200101-19-8000320 valid from 24.04.2019 to 23.04.2022.
5.
Respondent no. 3/
Insurance Company, in its written statement has admitted that offending vehicle was insured with it at the time of accident.
It is further submitted that IO in collusion with the petitioners, injured and driver and owner of the offending vehicle falsely implicated the vehicle in the accident.
No CCTV footage has been collected by the IO.
Deceased had died due to some unknown vehicle.
The petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation.

ISSUES:
6. After completion of pleadings, issues were framed by this Tribunal on 28.04.2022:

1. Whether deceased M. Vijayan S/o K. Kunhi Raman expired due to injuries suffered in road traffic accident on 26.12.2019 at about 08:10 PM, Rithala Metro Station CISF in front of Bairak road due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e.
HR-7CR-0123 (car XUV) which was being driven by driver Sh. Sanjeev Kumar S/o Babu Lal Ram on the said date, time and place ?

OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioner/injured is entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP.

13. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
& Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

Therefore, the case does not warrant any other best evidence.

Keeping in view the facts & evidence produced by the petitioner, it has proved on record that the said accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent no.1, as a result of which, the deceased lost his life.
16. The FIR has been lodged against the respondent no.1 and he has faced criminal charges of causing death and injuries by rash and negligent driving in the said accident.

Respondent No. 1 Driver and Respondent no. 2 being the owner of the offending car are jointly and severely liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Keeping in view the facts & evidence produced by the petitioner, it has proved on record that the said accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent no.1, as a result of which, the deceased lost his life.
16. The FIR has been lodged against the respondent no.1 and he has faced criminal charges of causing death and injuries by rash and negligent driving in the said accident.
Therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
COMPENSATION:
19.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death :
(a) age of the deceased;
(b) income of the deceased; and the (c) the number of dependents.
20. The issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
MACT Case No. 301/2020 (FIR no. 338/19) Shahney Vijayan & Anr. V. Sanjeev Kumar & Ors.
Page no. 7 of 17 (i) additions/deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and (iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference of the age of the deceased.
21.
Hence, the multiplier of "11" would be applicable in view of pronouncement made in case titled as Sarla Verma (supra).
26.
Considering the fact that deceased was aged about 52 years and 4 months of age at the time of accident and was not having a permanent job at that time, future prospects @ 10% has to be awarded in favour of petitioners in view of recent pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, as well as in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in appeal Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pooja & Ors, in MAC APP No. 798/2011.
The deceased was married and there are two claimants/ dependants upon him.
Thus, there are two dependants and there has to be deduction of "one third (1/3)", as per the mandate of Sarla Verma (supra).
After the judgment passed in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (supra)
and recent judgment titled as New India Assurance Company Limited v. Somwati & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 3093 of 2020 the petitioners are not entitled to be compensated under this head.
